requirements.statement: FS0 Governance SHALL implement the lifecycle Design Proposal -> Design -> Plan -> Build -> accepted repository state, with Design, Plan, and Build represented as distinct governed work.
Design SHALL use Audit, Normalize, Accept; Plan SHALL use Analyze, Specify, Accept; and Build SHALL use Implement, Verify, Accept.

Each governed Design, Plan, and Build work item SHALL have stable identity, explicit predecessor, explicit scope, material exclusions where applicable, candidate result, completion conditions, explicit acceptance or rejection, provenance, and bounded authorization.

Design SHALL consume a non-authoritative Design Proposal, audit accepted authority and relevant repository state, normalize persistent normative semantics into identified requirements, and explicitly accept or reject the normative delta.

Plan SHALL consume accepted Design authority, define realization intent including affected artifacts, Conformance work, Assurance work, dependencies, sequencing, and bounded Build scope, and SHALL NOT create or amend normative semantics.

Build SHALL consume an accepted Plan, implement only authorized Plan work, produce required evidence, invoke required Conformance and Assurance, verify completion, and SHALL NOT invent Design semantics or Plan intent.
Semantic defects SHALL route to Design, realization-intent defects SHALL route to Plan, and implementation defects SHALL route to Build.

Governance acceptance SHALL be explicit, attributable, traceable, candidate-specific, and distinct from merge state, issue closure, Conformance success, Assurance findings, review approval, workflow success, and tool declarations.
A Governance acceptance decision SHALL depend only on authority accepted before the candidate acquires any authority produced by that acceptance.
A governed work item SHALL authorize only its explicit scope, and completion or acceptance SHALL NOT independently authorize unrelated or successor work.
For the FS0 GitHub binding, each Design, Plan, or Build acceptance record SHALL be a structured machine-readable GitHub issue comment attached to that stage's governed-work issue.
Every machine-readable acceptance comment SHALL use marker repo-spec-acceptance:v1 followed by exactly one fenced JSON object using the Design-defined acceptance-record envelope and enum values.

A governance-acceptance record SHALL use schema_version 1, record_type governance-acceptance, stage design|plan|build, and disposition accepted|rejected, and SHALL contain acceptance_id, work_id, candidate_id, actor, evidence, decision_timestamp, and resulting_accepted_state where applicable.

A bootstrap-acceptance record SHALL use schema_version 1, record_type bootstrap-acceptance, stage bootstrap, and disposition accepted|rejected, and SHALL identify the exact candidate revision plus bootstrap verification and semantic-audit evidence.
For repository-changing work, candidate_id SHALL resolve to an exact Git commit SHA.

Accepted repository state SHALL be represented by refs/heads/accepted plus a matching valid acceptance record; the accepted ref SHALL move only after the applicable explicit acceptance decision exists.
Default-branch position, merge state, pull-request state, review state, comment state, and workflow state SHALL NOT independently create accepted repository state.
Initial bootstrap acceptance SHALL be recorded on a dedicated external bootstrap provenance issue and SHALL NOT be represented as FS0-governed Design, Plan, or Build work.

Technical write permission SHALL be treated only as capability and SHALL NOT enlarge Governance authorization; privileged mutation SHALL remain bounded by accepted authority, accepted Plan, and authorized Build scope.
After FS0 cutover, every persistent framework change SHALL occur through FS0 Governance and no bootstrap-only mechanism SHALL independently create accepted framework state.

Design Normalize and Assurance SHALL be capable of identifying materially compound obligations, ambiguity, contradiction, duplication, inappropriate implementation leakage, and missing semantic ownership.
